title: A quantum-gravitational explanation of the origin of the universe

concept.text: Strings 2000 problem 2 (proposed by Edward Witten): how can quantum gravity help explain the origin of the universe? Sources given: https://preskill.caltech.edu/millennium.html ; https://aip.brightspotcdn.com/PTO.v54.i10.14_2.online.pdf ; https://x.com/martinmbauer/status/1779906631003697211.

page.title: Quantum cosmology of the origin of the universe
page.definition: Quantum cosmology treats the universe’s geometry and matter as a single quantum system. A theory of cosmic origin would account for the universe’s initial conditions or earliest evolution and predict an observable consequence, such as a feature in the spectrum of primordial fluctuations. The no-boundary proposal sums over geometries that close off smoothly to the past and assigns probabilities to possible cosmic histories. Some loop quantum cosmology models instead describe a bounce from contraction to expansion.

goal.need: Cosmologists can trace much of the universe’s evolution from its first few seconds to the present. The equations of general relativity require initial conditions as input. A theory of those conditions could explain which early histories were likely and why the universe had the density fluctuations from which galaxies grew. The cosmic microwave background can test such an explanation only where competing initial states leave distinguishable patterns.

statements.body: Strings 2000 selection panel: Michael Duff, David Gross and Edward Witten
statements.quote: How can quantum gravity help explain the origin of the universe?
a complete cosmological theory of initial conditions is needed in addition to dynamical physical laws.

completion.title: Observations discriminate a quantum-gravity account of cosmic origin from specified alternatives.
completion.criterion: An explicit quantum-gravity account of the universe's initial conditions or earliest evolution yields the observed expanding universe and a quantitative prediction tied to that origin account. Cosmological observations support that prediction in a comparison that discriminates the account from specified alternatives, with parameter and approximation uncertainties included. Agreement with an inflationary spectrum alone is insufficient.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional operational test without an externally adopted discovery threshold.
completion.basis: Searched the Strings 2000 problem list, Connecting Quarks with the Cosmos, and quantum-cosmology reviews for an agreed completion test or numerical discovery threshold; none was found. This provisional test joins the initial-conditions goal to the requirement for an observational foundation discussed by Chataignier, Kiefer and Moniz.

milestones.title: A quantum-cosmological state satisfies the Wheeler–DeWitt constraint with an explicit origin prescription.
milestones.criterion: In canonical quantum geometrodynamics, specify the boundary conditions that encode the proposed origin. Construct a nonzero wave function Ψ of spatial geometry and matter that satisfies those conditions and the Wheeler–DeWitt constraint ĤΨ = 0.
milestones.set_by: Canonical quantum-cosmology constraint, stated by Hartle and Hawking in the abstract of Wave function of the Universe. This test applies to canonical wave-function formulations.
milestones.threshold_quote: The wave function obeys the Wheeler-DeWitt second-order functional differential equation.

milestones.title: A quantum-cosmology model has a bounded matter-density operator at its classical big-bang singularity.
milestones.criterion: For a cosmological model whose classical matter density diverges, construct the corresponding self-adjoint density operator on the physical Hilbert space, the space of states satisfying the quantum constraints. Show that the operator is bounded there, so that a single finite upper bound on density applies to every normalized physical state.
milestones.set_by: Bounded-observable diagnostic used in loop quantum cosmology by Ashtekar, Corichi and Singh, section V A; assessed by Thébault, section 6.2, criterion SR1. This is a sufficient local diagnostic, not a general test of cosmic origin.
milestones.threshold_quote: The sufficient condition we will identify is the boundedness of self-adjoint operators on the physical Hilbert space whose classical correlates are divergent

milestones.title: A quantum-origin state predicts expanding classical spacetime under the WKB classicality condition.
milestones.criterion: For a semiclassical branch Ψ = exp[(W + iS)/ℏ], show that (∇W)² ≪ (∇S)² in the proposed classical regime, with gradients contracted using the model’s configuration-space metric. Here W controls the amplitude and S the phase. Show that S obeys the classical Hamilton–Jacobi equation to leading order and that the momenta obtained from its gradient describe a history with increasing scale factor.
milestones.set_by: WKB classicality convention in quantum cosmology, reviewed by Lehners, section 2.4, equation (76), and implemented in Hartle, Hawking and Hertog's no-boundary models, section III B.
milestones.threshold_quote: the amplitude of the wave function should vary slowly compared to its phase.

milestones.title: A quantum-origin account yields a quantitative prediction suitable for a discriminating observational test.
milestones.criterion: Derive a quantitative cosmological observable from the proposed quantum origin and subsequent evolution. Parameterize uncertainties from the quantum state, the choice of quantization and the approximations. Specify the competing accounts and identify the feature of the observable that distinguishes their predictions.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional synthesis of Bojowald's effective-theory criterion and Chataignier, Kiefer and Moniz's observational requirement. No externally adopted criterion for this final theoretical step was found in those reviews.

milestones.title: A quantum-origin model recovers quantum field theory on its emergent classical spacetime.
milestones.criterion: In a regime where the model predicts a classical spacetime, derive the evolution of field perturbations from the quantum cosmological state. At leading order, recover the dynamics of quantum field theory on that same geometry. In a Schrödinger description, the perturbation state must obey the time-dependent Schrödinger equation with the field Hamiltonian for that background.
milestones.set_by: Halliwell and Hartle, criterion 4 for no-boundary integration contours, also implemented for cosmological perturbations by Chataignier, Kiefer and Moniz.
milestones.threshold_quote: the correct field theory in curved spacetime should be reproduced in this spacetime

not_found: No observational result satisfying the provisional completion test was found.

results.detail: The numerical illustration additionally assumes a vanishing wave function at a = 0. The paper leaves the determinant calculation that would fix the exact small-a behavior from the path integral unevaluated.
results.quote:
It implies not only the Wheeler-DeWitt equation but
also the boundary conditions which determine the

results.finding: In one closed minisuperspace model, the no-boundary ground state has an expanding de Sitter WKB branch for Ha > 1.

results.finding: In one closed radiation minisuperspace model, an excited state's tunneling probability per traversal has low-energy suppression exp[−2/(3H²)].
results.detail: The estimate uses semiclassical barrier penetration at small positive cosmological constant and energies well below the barrier height.
results.quote:
We can calculate the tunneling probability for small A,

results.finding: In one solvable no-boundary model, one expanding classical history, empty de Sitter, remains KS-allowable indefinitely.
results.detail: The large-scale-factor history relation is compared with an independently calculated KS boundary. The comparison tests saddle allowability along classical histories.

results.finding: Across eight slow-roll potential families, KS-allowable no-boundary trajectories predict a CMB tensor-to-scalar ratio r ≲ 0.08.
results.detail: The authors overlay existing CMB constraints and discuss the tunneling state’s KS failure. They supply no separate quantitative r prediction for the tunneling state.
results.quote:

results.finding: Hybrid LQC with a non-oscillatory vacuum lowers minimum χ² by about 1.7 versus ΛCDM in one Planck 2018 CMB dataset including lensing.
results.detail: The cutoff was fixed at the peak found using the same dataset. The χ² improvement is a fit comparison. A classical kinetic-dominance model can also produce similar infrared suppression.
results.quote: This improvement is also discussed in Refs.

results.finding: Across three models fit to Planck 2015, BAO, and BICEP2–Keck–Planck data, the full-multipole fit disfavors holographic cosmology by about 2.2σ versus ΛCDM with running.
results.detail: The two-loop expansion loses reliability at low multipoles, where the predicted spectra differ most. Within the adopted multipole cut, the data provide no significant Bayesian preference.
results.quote:
The χ2 of the ﬁt indicates that HC is disfavoured
at about 2.2σ relative to ΛCDM with running, when we
consider all multipoles.

results.finding: One solvable loop quantum cosmology model has a matter-density upper bound of about 0.41 times the Planck density for every normalized physical state.
results.detail: The result covers the volume-symmetric, zero-offset lattice sector. The supplied document is an arXiv preprint. It identifies Ref. [3], a peer-reviewed Physical Review D paper, as having already proved the same bound for either density ordering.
results.quote:
In this model, it was shown that
ρcrit ≈ 0.41ρp, where ρp is the Planck density.

results.finding: For one expanding no-boundary history sampled at 200 points, both WKB derivative ratios decreased exponentially with the number of e-folds.
results.detail: The minisuperspace metric is indefinite, so componentwise suppression alone does not establish the contracted inequality if the phase contributions nearly cancel.
results.quote:
Thus, as a function of the number of e-folds N, the wavefunction becomes classical expo-
nentially fast.

results.finding: In one biaxial Bianchi IX model, the four-ball no-boundary branch yields expanding WKB histories. The numerical classicality plot uses a 100-fold phase-gradient threshold.
results.detail: The 100-fold cutoff is a plotting convention. The asymptotic calculation establishes the hierarchy at fixed squashing. The expanding solution is one of two conjugate branches of the time-neutral state.
results.quote:

results.finding: In one flat loop quantum cosmology model, first-order perturbations recover the field Schrödinger equation on the emergent classical FLRW spacetime.
results.detail: The derivation neglects perturbation backreaction. Equation (4.12) gives the state evolution, and comparison with (4.13) identifies the field Hamiltonian on the dressed metric, which approaches the classical FLRW metric at late times.
results.quote:
Again, this is an exact equivalence between our truncated LQG and the theory of quantu m
ﬁelds on a smooth FLR W geometry determined by ˜a and ˜p(φ).

results.finding: Two loop quantum cosmology quantizations predict low-multipole CMB temperature power suppression relative to ΛCDM at about 140 total e-folds.
results.detail: The hybrid and dressed metric temperature spectra are very similar when the dressed metric model has one additional e-fold. The authors leave the statistical significance of the comparison with Planck data for future analysis.

results.detail: The benchmark saturates Planck’s quadrupole constraint. The distinct polarization test uses off-diagonal correlations, while cosmic variance exceeds the predicted changes in diagonal CMB spectra.
